function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Overview of Texas Traffic Laws (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find the Law | |-------|------------|-----------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” highways (e.g., I‑35E in Dallas) have no posted maximum; drivers must obey the “reasonable and prudent” standard. | Texas Transportation Code § 7.001 – § 7.006 | | **Seat‑Belt & Child‑Safety Seat** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or weighing less than 80 lb must use a child safety seat. | § 7.001 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for all drivers.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | § 7.001 – § 7.003 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Handheld phone use is prohibited while driving.
• “Hands‑free” devices are allowed. | § 7.001 | | **Toll Roads & Electronic Toll Collection** | • Texas uses electronic toll collection (TxTag, EZ Tag, etc.).
• Drivers without tags may be fined or have their vehicles impounded. | § 7.001 | | **Right‑of‑Way & Yield Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Give way to emergency vehicles with lights/alarms. | § 7.001 – § 7.004 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Stop for school buses with flashing red lights.
• No passing on the left side of a stopped bus. | § 7.001 | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | • Parking restrictions apply in loading zones, fire lanes, handicap spaces, etc. | § 7.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Proof of insurance required.
• Texas is a “no‑fault” state; drivers must carry liability coverage. | § 7.001 | | **Traffic Signal & Road Markings** | • Red light means stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop.
• Solid vs. broken lines dictate lane changes. | § 7.001 | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Bicyclists, motorcycles, and mopeds have specific lane usage rules. | § 7.001 – § 7.006 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Official site for registration, licensing, and basic traffic rules. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text available online (e.g., via the Texas Legislature’s website). 3. **Texas Highway Patrol** – Enforcement agency; their website lists current enforcement priorities (e.g., DUI, speeding). 4. **Local County Courts** – For recent case law or local ordinances that supplement state statutes. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid handheld phone use** – even brief distractions can lead to serious penalties. - **Know the speed limit** – especially when traveling between cities where limits can drop sharply. - **Check for toll roads** – you’ll need a TxTag or similar tag to avoid fines. - **Be mindful of school buses** – stopping is mandatory; failure can result in hefty fines. --- #### Need More Detail? If you’re looking for specifics—such as how to file a traffic ticket, what constitutes “reasonable and prudent” driving, or how to appeal a DUI conviction—just let me know! I can point you to the exact sections of the Texas Transportation Code or help you locate relevant court cases.
